Governor-elect Benson says she will open governor’s office to FOIA requests

By James Felton
Published: Nov. 4, 2026 at 6:10 PM EST|Updated: 11 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:08
Instaread

LANSING, Mich. — Democrats are in line to take control of all three branches of Michigan state government in January once election results are certified, with Jocelyn Benson set to take office as governor alongside Democratic majorities in both the state House and Senate.

The midterm elections delivered results for many Democrats across the country and in Michigan.

Benson, a Democrat, will be sworn in Jan. 1 and will inherit a Legislature controlled by Democrats in both chambers.

Benson said she met Wednesday with Gov. Gretchen Whitmer. She thanked Whitmer for her leadership, friendship and service to the people of Michigan, and she expects a smooth transition into her new role.

“Last night, Michiganders came together across geographic, racial, partisan lines around the issues that matter most to families. And today, we get to work delivering for them,” Benson said.

Benson said voters gave her administration a mandate.

“Michiganders have given us a clear mandate to work for them, to lower costs, to grow our economy, to improve our public schools, and get things done. And we will meet that mandate working hand in hand with our legislative leaders, and everyone in the Legislature on both sides of the aisle, frankly, from day one. Because we want to implement a vision for Michigan that includes everyone,” Benson said.

She said work begins Wednesday on identifying where the administration can deliver relief early in its term.

“Today, we will begin identifying where we can deliver quick relief in the early days of our new term, beginning with the bills families feel every month. We will work with experts, community leaders, and people who know what’s broken and how to work with us to fix it,” Benson said.

Benson said she will make the governor’s office open to Freedom of Information Act requests once she is sworn in.

“Once I am sworn in as the next governor of Michigan, we will voluntarily make the governor’s office open to FOIA,” Benson said.

FOIA stands for the Freedom of Information Act. It grants the public a legal right to request access to government agency records. Michigan is one of two states that exempts the governor’s office from FOIA requests.

Benson said she wants a government that shows up for people when they need it and gets out of the way when they don’t.

“No matter who you are, or where you live, or who you worship, or who you voted for, I want you to know that you have a place in our vision, in our Michigan, and in our future,” Benson said.

U.S. Rep. John James posted a video to his Facebook page after conceding his defeat to Benson.

“Thank you, Michigan. The best is still yet to come and serving you has been the honor of a lifetime,” James said in part. “I’m never going to relent in working with anyone and everyone for a greater, more prosperous and more free Michigan.”
